identity.title: Closing the feedback-feeding loop of the radio galaxy 3C 84

paper_type_evidence.quote: This paper is based on re-processing the data taken for ALMA project 2017.0.01257.S of which the original data were published by Nagai et al.
To improve the calibration of these data, we reprocessed the archival ALMA visibility data.

redshift_or_distance.value: z = 0.01756 (V_hel = 5264 km/s); luminosity distance 76.2 Mpc; 0.1 arcsec = 36 pc

evidence.quote: NGC 1275 is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus cluster and hosts the radio-loud AGN 3C 84 (Perseus A).
In this paper we assume a redshift for NGC 1275 of $z = 0.01756; V_{\rm hel} = 5264$ km s$^{-1}$.
Assuming a Hubble constant of $H_\circ = 69.6$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, $\Omega_{\rm M} = 0.286$ and $\Omega_{\rm vac} = 0.714$, this gives
a luminosity distance of 76.2 Mpc.

distance_source.value: assumed redshift with H0 = 69.6 km/s/Mpc, Omega_M = 0.286, Omega_vac = 0.714 (no citation given)

evidence.quote: NGC 1275 is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus cluster and hosts the radio-loud AGN 3C 84 (Perseus A).
In this paper we assume a redshift for NGC 1275 of $z = 0.01756; V_{\rm hel} = 5264$ km s$^{-1}$.
Assuming a Hubble constant of $H_\circ = 69.6$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, $\Omega_{\rm M} = 0.286$ and $\Omega_{\rm vac} = 0.714$, this gives
a luminosity distance of 76.2 Mpc.

question.value: Do kpc-sized cold molecular gas filaments in NGC 1275 (host of 3C 84) flow onto and feed the circumnuclear disc (CND), closing the feedback-feeding loop of the AGN?

evidence.quote: Here we present high-resolution ALMA observations that clearly show that kpc-sized filaments of molecular gas are indeed accreting onto the CND.
no observations were yet able to simultaneously trace both these inner structures and explore, with high enough spatial resolution, whether any connection between them exists.
This work is based on re-processing of the ALMA observations carried out under project number 2017.0.01257.S and which were published in original form by Nagai et al. (cite: Nagai19)
We present the results of re-processed CO(2-1) ALMA observations of the cold molecular gas in the central regions of NGC 1275

angular_resolution.value: beam 0.19 x 0.10 arcsec (P.A. = 4.8 deg), 68 x 36 pc

evidence.quote: The beam size is 0$\overset{\prime\prime}{.}$19 $\times$ 0$\overset{\prime\prime}{.}$10 (P.A. = 4$\overset{\circ}{.}$8), corresponding to 68 $\times$ 36 pc
The largest recoverable scale of the ALMA array used in the observations is 1$\overset{\prime\prime}{.}$3.

method.value: Single phase-only self-calibration of pipeline-calibrated visibilities using a point model for 3C 84

evidence.quote: Before attempting to improve the bandpass calibration, we applied a single phase-only self-calibration to the visibilities using a point model for 3C 84.

assumptions.value: 3C 84 is a point source at the phase centre for the model

evidence.quote: using a point model for 3C 84.

analysis_steps.goal: re-derive the bandpass using 3C 84 itself, iteratively

method.value: Bandpass solution from 3C 84 using only baselines longer than 500 klambda; line emission modelled and subtracted from the uv data, then bandpass redetermined; done twice

evidence.quote: selecting only the $uv$ data on baselines longer than 500 k$\lambda$ in order to reduce the impact of extended line emission.
was done twice, after which successive iterations did not improve the quality of the data anymore.

key_parameters.value: Baselines > 500 klambda, spatial scales smaller than about 0.4 arcsec

evidence.quote: This limit means that for the bandpass calibration we only consider spatial scales smaller than $\sim$0$\overset{\prime\prime}{.}$4

assumptions.value: Line emission is much weaker than the 3C 84 continuum so the bandpass error it induces is small

evidence.quote: the level of the continuum is much higher than that of the line emission and therefore the errors induced by this way of calibrating the data are small.

validation.value: Comparison of position-velocity plots of the CND from archival and re-processed data; good agreement a few beams from 3C 84

evidence.quote: comparison of the emission only a few beams away from 3C 84 shows very good correspondence between the two data sets

method.value: Imaging with natural weighting, 13.1 km/s channels, Hanning smoothing

evidence.quote: was made using natural weighting and with channels of 13.1 km s$^{-1}$ wide to which Hanning smoothing was applied

key_parameters.value: Velocity resolution 26.1 km/s; beam 0.19 x 0.10 arcsec; noise 0.36 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: giving a velocity resolution of 26.1 km s$^{-1}$.
the noise level in the channels is 0.36 mJy beam$^{-1}$

validation.value: Noise improved by a factor 3 over the original cube

evidence.quote: This is an improvement of a factor 3 over that of the original data cube

analysis_steps.goal: make moment images (integrated line and velocity field)

method.value: SoFiA-2 Smooth+Clip finder builds a mask from merged smoothed-cube masks; mask applied to the original cube to compute moments

evidence.quote: We have used the Smooth+Clip finder as implemented in Sofia-2 to create a mask including all the emission to apply to the data cube for the calculations of the moments.

key_parameters.value: Spatial Gaussian kernels 0, 3, 6, 12, 24 pixels; velocity boxcar kernels 0, 3, 7 channels; noise cutoff 4 sigma

evidence.quote: The scales of the spatial Gaussian kernels we used are 0, 3, 6, 12 and 24 pixels and of the velocity boxcar kernels 0, 3, and 7 channels.
The noise cutoff used was 4 $\sigma$.

analysis_steps.goal: examine kinematics along filaments and the CND

method.value: Position-velocity diagrams along selected position angles and along filaments, plus velocity-field inspection, to judge infall onto the CND

evidence.quote: position-velocity plots along two streams that seem to feed the CND.
shows the position-velocity plot along position angle 90$^\circ$ after integrating the data cube in declination.

key_parameters.value: PA 90 deg slice through the CND; PA 150 deg along filament D centred 0.3 arcsec W of the centre

evidence.quote: The left panel shows the kinematics of the CND along position angle 90$^\circ$.

assumptions.value: Filaments pointing toward 3C 84 with organised E-W kinematics are infalling, not pushed outward by the N-S jets

evidence.quote: something that would not be expected if the gas is pushed outwards by the jets which are oriented N-S.

analysis_steps.goal: measure flux integrals and derive H2 masses

method.value: Flux integrals of the full field, CND and filaments A, B, C converted to H2 mass with a CO-to-H2 conversion factor and a CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) ratio

evidence.quote: The flux integral of the CND is $22.2 \pm 1$ Jy km s$^{-1}$
If one instead assumes $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 0.8\ M_\odot$/(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$), which could more appropriate for conditions found near an AGN, all masses decrease by a factor 5.4.

key_parameters.value: alpha_CO = 4.3 Msun/(K km/s pc^2) and S_CO(2-1) = 2.4 S_CO(1-0) (standard ISM); alternative alpha_CO = 0.8

evidence.quote: Using $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 4.3\ M_\odot$/(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$) and $S_{\rm CO(2-1)} = 2.4\ S_{\rm CO(1-0)}$

assumptions.value: Standard Galactic ISM conversion factor as default; AGN-like lower factor as alternative

evidence.quote: It is a priori not clear which CO–to–H$_2$ conversion factor to use since the conditions in the molecular gas are likely quite different from that in the standard galaxy ISM(cite: Lim17).

assumptions.value: Most CO(2-1) emission recovered by the array

evidence.quote: which suggests that we have likely recovered most of the CO(2-1) emission.

validation.value: Comparison of flux integrals with the SMA result of Ho et al.

evidence.quote: which roughly corresponds to our filaments A and B which have a combined flux integral of $38.3 \pm 1.9$ Jy km s$^{-1}$.

analysis_steps.goal: estimate the gas infall rate onto the CND

method.value: Mdot = M_gas / t_dyn = M_gas (r/v)^-1 for filament gas within r = 0.7 arcsec (~250 pc), with infall velocity 200 km/s

evidence.quote: $$\begin{equation} \dot{M} = \frac{M_{\rm gas}}{t_{\rm dyn}} = M_{\rm gas} \cdot \left(\frac{r}{v}\right)^{-1} \end{equation}$$
If we assume such an infall velocity, this gives an estimated infall rate of about 200 $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$.

key_parameters.value: Gas mass of about 5e8 Msun inside radius 0.7 arcsec (~250 pc) for alpha_CO = 4.3; v = 200 km/s

evidence.quote: is about $5 \times 10^8$ $M_\odot$ for $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 4.3\ M_\odot$/(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$).

assumptions.value: Infall velocity 200 km/s taken from radial infall models; same conversion factor for filaments and CND

evidence.quote: Assuming the same CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor for the filaments and the CND and the infall velocity of 200 km s$^{-1}$ used above

validation.value: Compared with cooling rates from the literature (X-ray cooling flow, Halpha filaments)

evidence.quote: This compares reasonably well with the disposition rate of at least 30 $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ of the X-ray cooling flow

findings_qualitative.value: Inner and Western filaments split into several thinner filaments with different kinematics, more complex than seen at 1 kpc resolution

evidence.quote: split into several thinner filaments with different kinematics, thus revealing that the distribution and the kinematics of the molecular gas are much more complex than perceived from their data.

findings_qualitative.value: Outer CND shows unsettled, non-regular kinematics consistent with ongoing gas accretion onto the CND

evidence.quote: This on-going formation of the CND is further confirmed by the non-regular kinematics of the outer regions of the CND

findings_qualitative.value: Accretion is organised in filamentary channels (not chaotic), though individual filaments carry angular momentum

evidence.quote: However, the accretion itself is not chaotic but organised in the form of filamentary channels along which cold gas is funnelled into the central regions.

claims.hypothesis: Do kpc-scale cold molecular filaments flow onto the circumnuclear disc and feed the AGN?
claims.experiment: Re-processed archival ALMA CO(2-1) data with improved bandpass calibration at 50 pc resolution; moment maps and position-velocity diagrams
claims.result: Filaments connect in position and velocity to the CND; the CND outskirts show asymmetric, unsettled kinematics
claims.finding: Cold filaments flow onto and build up the CND, closing the feedback-feeding loop

evidence.quote: how kpc-sized cold gas filaments resulting from jet-induced cooling of cluster gas are flowing towards the galaxy centre and how they feed the circumnuclear accretion disc (100 pc diameter) of the SMBH

claims.hypothesis: Does a different bandpass calibration scheme remove the artefacts in the archival cube?
claims.experiment: Bandpass derived from 3C 84 on long baselines with iterative line subtraction, then re-imaged
claims.result: Noise lowered by a factor 3 (0.36 vs 1 mJy/beam) and imaging artefacts eliminated, except inside about 0.2 arcsec of 3C 84
claims.finding: Re-processed cube is of much improved quality and recovers the filaments

evidence.quote: using a different bandpass calibration scheme (see Methods) which resulted in eliminating the imaging artefacts and thus in much improved image quality and much lower noise levels

claims.hypothesis: Is the filamentary structure more complex than seen at 1 kpc resolution?
claims.experiment: Integrated line emission and velocity-field maps from the new cube
claims.result: Inner and Western filaments split into several thinner filaments with different kinematics
claims.finding: Distribution and kinematics of molecular gas are much more complex than previously perceived

evidence.quote: split into several thinner filaments with different kinematics, thus revealing that the distribution and the kinematics of the molecular gas are much more complex than perceived from their data.

claims.hypothesis: What is the cold gas infall rate onto the CND relative to the cooling flow?
claims.experiment: Mdot = M_gas/t_dyn with filament H2 masses, v = 200 km/s, and two CO-to-H2 conversion factors
claims.result: Infall rate of about 20-200 Msun/yr depending on the conversion factor
claims.finding: Rate is comparable to the X-ray cooling flow and Halpha cooling rates, but strongly dependent on the uncertain conversion factor

evidence.quote: Although there is a large uncertainty in which CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor to use, we estimate that the disposition rate of cold gas onto the CND to be in the range 20–200 $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$

why_this_data.value: Earlier data lacked the resolution to link filaments to the CND, and the published ALMA cube was limited by bandpass artefacts

evidence.quote: the relatively low spatial resolution of their data do not allow to separate these large filaments from the CND and to establish whether the filaments are actually accreting onto the CND.

why_this_method.value: 3C 84 is itself the brightest calibrator on the sky so it is used as the bandpass calibrator

evidence.quote: there are no calibrator sources on the sky that are significantly stronger than 3C 84

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Standard ALMA pipeline bandpass (as used by Nagai et al.) rejected because the bandpass calibrator is 1 Jy versus 7 Jy for 3C 84 and observed only 5 minutes

evidence.quote: the flux density of the bandpass calibrator used (J0237+2848) is about 1 Jy while that of 3C 84 is roughly 7 Jy.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Lower alpha_CO = 0.8 considered as an AGN-appropriate alternative to the standard 4.3

evidence.quote: If one instead assumes $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 0.8\ M_\odot$/(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$), which could more appropriate for conditions found near an AGN, all masses decrease by a factor 5.4.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Bandpass line-subtraction iterations stopped after two rounds when quality no longer improved

evidence.quote: was done twice, after which successive iterations did not improve the quality of the data anymore.

limitations_admitted.value: Final cube likely incorrect within about 0.2 arcsec of 3C 84 (inner CND)

evidence.quote: our final data cube is likely incorrect within $\sim$0$\overset{\prime\prime}{.}$2 from 3C 84 (i.e. the inner part of the CND)

limitations_admitted.value: Absorption against the 3C 84 continuum cannot be studied because the calibration removes it

evidence.quote: Another implication of our calibration method is that any absorption signature that would possibly be present is calibrated away

limitations_admitted.value: Large uncertainty in the CO-to-H2 conversion factor and thus in masses and accretion rates

evidence.quote: Although there is a large uncertainty in which CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor to use

limitations_admitted.value: Eastern filament lies beyond the half-power point of the ALMA primary beam, so only faint emission is detected there

evidence.quote: is located well beyond the half-power point of the ALMA primary beam and only some faint emission is detected at that location in our observations.

referee_caveats_inferred: Infall is inferred from morphology and position-velocity connections; line-of-sight geometry could allow outflow, and no dynamical model or fit is shown
Infall rate depends on an assumed 200 km/s velocity taken from older models and on a conversion factor uncertain by a factor 5.4
Bandpass derived from 3C 84 with iterative line subtraction may bias faint extended emission; no quantified test of fidelity beyond comparison with the archival cube
Mass and flux values lack stated primary-beam correction and systematic flux-scale error

data_public_as_stated.value: Archival ALMA visibilities; calibrated data cube available at a stated link or on request

evidence.quote: we reprocessed the archival ALMA visibility data.
The calibrated data cube is available from

code_released.value: No new code released; MIRIAD and SoFiA-2 are described as publicly available

evidence.quote: The data were reduced using the publicly available software Miriad(cite: Sault95) and Sofia-2(cite: Westmeier21).
